thread:
erin: getting multiple SEV reports — hosted /v1/generate p99 up ~3x since 07:12 UTC, customer-facing latency alerts firing :rotating_light:

mike: saw it on dashboards too, p95 ~600ms -> 2s, p99 ~1.2s -> 6s. Any recent deploys?

sre_bot: alert: latency_p99_generation > 4s for 3m (hosts affected: gpu-pool-3a).

erin: rollback window shows a model-weights hotflip deploy at 07:08 by @jess. tagging @jess to confirm.

jess: yep I rolled a redeploy of compile-kernel-optimizer at 07:07 to pick up a kernel patch. I can roll back but want quick mitigations first.

adil: quick triage: tail of traces shows long time in KV-cache eviction and swap-in on node gpu-pool-3a. Also high IO wait on those hosts. Could be kernel change changed page-touch pattern.

niko: confirmed: traces with trace_id 8a3f... show stall during cache_read -> backend_io read for large prompt lengths. Affected mostly >1024 token requests.

mike: customer reports are from a batch job generating embeddings and many long completion requests. Might be correlation with larger seq lengths.

erin: urgent mitigation plan: 1) apply rate-limiter rule to slow incoming >512 token requests for hosted tier for 30m; 2) enable fallback routing to low-memory optimized model variant (model-x-small-quant) for non-SLAs; 3) pin affected hosts out of LB; 4) roll back kernel patch if needed. Any objections?

jess: ok to push those. I can roll back in 10m but prefer to test fallback first.

adil: I will create a temporary rate-limit rule: 
```
POST /internal/rules/ratelimit
{
  "match": "request.seq_len > 512 && client.tier == 'hosted'",
  "action": "throttle: 20rps"
}
```
apply to region eu-west-1 and us-east-1, + allow whitelisted enterprise keys.

mike: also set CB (circuit-breaker) on the generation route to trip at 3s p99 window and fallback to model-x-small-quant or to queued response with 429. We should prefer model fallback to 429 for good UX.

niko: I'm deploying a routing policy change now: route-policy-id=rb-2026-09-fallback. Command: `rbctl apply --policy route-policy-id`

sre_bot: action_log: applied rate-limit rule rl-2026-09-11-01 by user:adil at 07:22 UTC.

adil: rate limit active. Metrics dashboard: incoming >512 token requests reduced by ~70% within 2 minutes. p95 improved to ~900ms, p99 still ~3.5s.

jess: routing policy deployed to send non-critical traffic to model-x-small-quant. Verified via logs: `router.match(seq_len>512) -> model-x-small-quant`

mike: good. For customers with strict latency SLAs we need immediate whitelisting — @erin can you coordinate support messages?

erin: on it. Pushing notification to status.redwood.ai: "We are mitigating elevated tail latency on generation endpoints. Non-SLA traffic may be routed to lower-memory model variants to restore latency. Investigating root cause."

adil: while rate-limit + fallback helped, hosts still showing IO wait; I recommend cordon + reboot of gpu-pool-3a nodes one-by-one to clear kernel state. Planning to cordon host gpu-3a-07 now.

jess: do we need rollback or can we avoid it? If reboot fixes kernel pages, we can avoid rollback.

niko: start cordon and reboot; I'll monitor traces.

sre_bot: incident: host_cordon gpu-3a-07 initiated by niko at 07:29 UTC.

adil: rebooted gpu-3a-07. post-reboot: IO wait dropped, KV-cache hit rate back up ~15%. p99 dropped to ~1.4s.

erin: customers reporting improvement, some still see occasional spikes.

mike: next step: schedule controlled rollback of kernel optimizer on canary hosts 1/3 to verify if regression was introduced. If we don't see regression after reboots, deprioritize rollback.

jess: initiating canary rollback on compile-kernel-optimizer to previous version on canary pool gpu-canary-1. Command: `deploy rollback compile-kernel-optimizer --to-tag v1.4.2 --target gpu-canary-1`

niko: canary results: no regressions on canary after 20m, KV-cache metrics stable.

adil: hypothesis: combination of kernel patch + high memory pressure from long-seq requests caused eviction storms. Mitigations we used: temporary token-length rate limit, routing fallback, cordon+reboot, canary rollback. Recommend these be captured in a short runbook.

erin: will open a support follow-up ticket to notify impacted customers with steps taken and ETA for permanent fix. Also creating post-incident TODOs:
- add a p99 guardrail that enforces automatic model-fallback when p99 > 3s for >5m
- add a hard circuit-breaker config for seq_len>1024 to return 413 or route to queued mode for non-SLA keys
- add metrics alert for KV-cache hit rate drop >10%

jess: I'll prepare a patch to make the kernel change opt-in and run longer soak tests.

mike: ops note: for future we should throttle large batched embedding jobs via a quota and suggest using smaller batch sizes or dedicated capacity.

erin: summary posted to #incidents and linked to ticket INC-2026-298. Thanks team :tada:

sre_bot: incident_resolved: p99 back to baseline for 15m. incident closed at 07:43 UTC.
